source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10 ("County and rural council nominations")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)

note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Omagh rural district, one member each, polled on 5 June 1952. Only Glenlark was contested, where an Independent opposed the outgoing Nationalist; 'Twenty-one Unionists and 17 Nationalists for Omagh Rural Council have been returned unopposed' (Strabane Chronicle, 24 May 1952, p. 3, which prints the full list of nominations, labels as printed). Ten new members came in unopposed. New member (U.). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Benchran' to Bancran (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1925-69 name the DED Bancran; the rounds were filed as Bencran (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Benchran (1952). This round was filed as 'Benchran', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (benchran) answers with a redirect to this one.
